rounds.title: The Rush Order
rounds.brief: Aurelle, a key customer, wants all 5,000 pendants of order AU-118 one week early, for a store launch. Decide by 2 p.m.

A.label: Full order early
A.text: All 5,000 in 1 week. Both lines run 12-hour shifts, 7 days a week.

B.label: Split the shipment
B.text: Ship the 3,000 that pass QC this week. Ship the other 2,000 on the original date.

C.label: Ask for a new date
C.text: Offer all 5,000 three days before the original date, with no extra overtime.

D.label: Polite no
D.text: Keep the original date for the full order.

cards.text: Normal output: 250 finished pendants a day. Line 1 plates, Line 2 polishes.
Both lines already run 2 shifts, 6 days a week.
A third shift needs 5 trained platers. We have 2.
cards.title: Third shift check

cards.text: Line 1 plating tank is overdue for service. It failed twice this year when it ran non-stop.
cards.title: Line 1 service log

cards.text: 3,100 of the 5,000 pendants are finished and waiting for final QC.
Original ship date: in 2 weeks. Aurelle now asks for all 5,000 in 1 week.
We ship to Aurelle by air: 3 days, door to door.
cards.title: Freight plan

cards.text: A rival factory offered Aurelle the same pendants for 10% less.
cards.title: Market chatter

cards.text: Aurelle buys about $2.4M from us a year.
Overtime costs 1.5 times normal pay. Overtime budget left this month: $6,000.
Our contract with Aurelle allows split shipments: up to 2 per order, no penalty.
cards.title: Contract terms

cards.text: A second air shipment costs about $3,500 extra.
cards.title: Freight cost

cards.text: This week, 4 of our 30 line workers are on approved leave.
Hours cap: 60 hours per person per week, overtime included. Line teams already work 48.
Last year, minor injuries tripled on the third 12-hour shift in a row.
cards.title: Fatigue data

cards.text: Some workers want extra overtime pay before the New Year.
cards.title: Shop-floor mood

cards.text: Customer rule: every shipment needs a QC certificate. No certificate, no delivery.
Final QC of 3,000 pieces takes 1 day. Pass rate this month: 98%.
Rushed batches last year had 3 times more plating defects.
cards.title: Defect history

cards.text: Aurelle rarely checks certificates on rush orders.
cards.title: QC rumor

stakeholders.name: Aurelle's buyer
stakeholders.text: Our store launch is on the 20th. 3,000 pieces would cover our top stores. The rest can follow on the original date.

stakeholders.name: Head of Production Planning
stakeholders.text: We can still finish the last 2,000 by the original date, even if a line stops for 2 days.

stakeholders.name: Head of Maintenance
stakeholders.text: The Line 1 tank is overdue. Run it non-stop this week and I would expect a breakdown.

stakeholders.name: QC Manager
stakeholders.text: I will not sign a certificate for parts we did not inspect.

stakeholders.name: Freight forwarder
stakeholders.text: Two air shipments are fine. Just book 48 hours ahead.

breaking_news.text: Maintenance: the Line 1 plating tank has failed. Line 1 is down for 48 hours.

right: Aurelle's stock at launch and their feedback
Zero injuries, nobody over the hours cap

A: Somehow it worked and nobody got hurt. Pure luck.
Line 1 broke down, tired crews made a reject batch, and two people got minor injuries.
B: Aurelle launched on time and placed a reorder.
The first flight left a day late. Aurelle was annoyed but kept the order.
C: Aurelle accepted the new date and thanked us for being honest.
Aurelle moved part of the order to another factory.
D: Aurelle complained to our Plant Director.

rounds.title: The Short Supply
rounds.brief: Only 600 of 1,000 kg of brass alloy arrived. The rest comes in 3 weeks. Decide how to use the 600 kg by 12 noon.

A.label: Equal cut
A.text: Every open order gets 60% of the metal it needs.

B.label: Due dates first
B.text: 450 kg to the two big orders due in 10 days, 150 kg to small orders. Nord waits.

C.label: Key account first
C.text: Hold 100 kg for Aurelle, our biggest customer. Then use the rest by due date.

D.label: Stop and wait
D.text: Pause production until the full 1,000 kg arrives.

trap.text: Supplier Kestrel Metals: we can deliver the missing 400 kg in 5 days if you sign a 3-year exclusive contract for all your brass alloy. Value: $6.5M. Answer in 2 hours.
trap.label: NO WAY BACK
trap.authority_card: Contracts over $1M need the Regional VP and Legal.

cards.text: Each product change on a line takes 4 hours of setup.
Lines 3 and 4 stand side by side in Building B, 2 minutes apart.
Metal waste: 2% on long runs, 6% when we switch products often.
cards.title: Scrap data

cards.text: Night shift says they can get more parts from the same kilos.
cards.title: Shift chatter

cards.text: 600 kg arrived today. The other 400 kg arrive in 3 weeks.
Aurelle and Mira Home: 450 kg, due in 10 days. Nord: 300 kg, due in 4 weeks. Small orders: 250 kg, flexible dates.
cards.title: Order book

cards.text: Last year, small-order customers accepted a 2-week delay 9 times out of 10.
cards.title: Delay history

cards.text: After the rush order, Aurelle placed a reorder: 100 kg more, due in 10 days.
After the rush order, Aurelle told our sales team the delivery felt chaotic.
Brass alloy price rose 8% this quarter.
cards.title: Price trend

cards.text: Contract approval: Plant Director up to $500k. Over $1M: Regional VP and Legal.
Late penalties on the two big orders: about $60k per week, from day 1.
Kestrel Metals may have money problems next year.
cards.title: Supplier gossip

cards.text: Line teams are tired after the rush order.
Weekend rule: a maintenance tech must reach any running line within 10 minutes.
If a line stops, 30 contract workers get no shift pay.
cards.title: Stop impact

cards.text: Some team leaders say an equal cut is the only fair way.
cards.title: Team mood

cards.text: Every order must use certified nickel-free alloy. No certificate, no shipment.
Mira Home audits our material certificates every quarter.
Kestrel's alloy is not yet certified nickel-free. Certification takes 6 weeks.
cards.title: Supplier certification

cards.text: One buyer said an equal cut would look fairer to all customers.
cards.title: Buyer's view

stakeholders.name: Plant Director
stakeholders.text: I can approve the allocation. A supplier contract that size is not mine. Take it to the Regional VP.

stakeholders.name: Head of Production
stakeholders.text: Long runs on the two big orders waste the least metal. Small orders can wait 2 weeks.

stakeholders.name: Legal
stakeholders.text: Never sign an exclusive deal in 2 hours.

stakeholders.name: Kestrel Metals sales rep
stakeholders.text: Other buyers want this slot. Decide fast.

stakeholders.name: Aurelle account manager
stakeholders.text: Aurelle is our biggest customer. Give them everything first.

right: Big orders shipped on time, with certificates
wrong: Number of customers who got some metal

A: Customers were patient this time. Penalties stayed small.
Both big orders shipped late. Penalties hit $120k.
B: Both big orders shipped on time. Small customers took the delay well.
A machine fault cost a day, but penalties stayed small.
C: Aurelle got its reorder and praised the factory.
Mira Home shipped 3 days late and complained.
D: The rest of the metal came early and orders caught up.
The lines sat idle and every order shipped late.

carry.rule: by R1 choice, never by luck
carry.client_note: Aurelle reorder (B, C) or Aurelle complaint (A)

small_call.text: Can Lines 3 and 4 share one maintenance tech this weekend? I need a yes or no today.

escalate.reply: Plant Director: That's your call. You don't need me for this.

quality_v2.evidence: -1 if no critical or key card matches the chosen option
quality_v2.rumor: -1 only if a rumor is the only evidence
quality_v2.measure: -1 if the measure does not fit
quality_v2.defended: +1 by host when the rationale makes a fair case (max 5)

trust_v2.call_fatigue: calls 3 and up get shorter, irritated replies

scoring.speed_note: only the main stamp sets Speed. The trap and the small call do not change Speed, only the time they cost.
announce_upfront: Ask the right people, not everyone
Every report and call costs time

table_rules.leader: cos if present, else rotates each round
table_rules.note: cos holds no data: owns the stamp, the clock view and the rationale draft

players.store: nickname only, deleted after the session

phone_only: stakeholder calls (phone filter, low volume, text always shown)
